paper_title: Spectra of axions emitted from main sequence stars
coupling_convention: g_agamma in GeV^-1, canonical axion-photon coupling
notes: This paper computes axion emission spectra from main sequence stars and the resulting Stellar Axion Background (StAB). Section 3.1 derives exclusion limits on g_aγγ vs m_a from the cosmic X-ray background (CXB) using NuSTAR data. However, the paper explicitly states (Fig. 7 caption and Section 3.1 text): 'our limits are based on different assumptions from that of these earlier works' and 'The limits that we found lie in a parameter space that is already ruled out, mainly by limits based on relic axions from the early universe [66, 68] and partially by limits from gravitationally bound axions around the Sun [127, 128].' The paper does NOT present a NEW exclusion limit that improves upon or supersedes existing constraints. Instead, it derives limits in a region already excluded by prior work (CAST, globular clusters, early universe bounds). Figure 7 shows the exclusion region, but this is a theoretical prediction based on StAB decay, not an independent experimental measurement. The paper is primarily a theoretical/computational study of stellar axion production and the resulting diffuse background, not an experimental exclusion limit paper. No numerical data points can be reliably extracted from Fig. 7 without access to the underlying figure data, and the paper's own statement that these limits are subsumed by existing bounds makes them non-novel. Extraction confidence is low because: (1) no new measured limit is claimed, (2) the coupling type is clear (AxionPhoton) but (3) the data cannot be reliably digitized from the figure, and (4) the limits are acknowledged as non-competitive. | selector: figure_vision (sole candidate) | Vision: Figure 7 shows exclusion limits on axion parameter space (m_a, g_agamma) at 95% confidence level derived from chi-squared goodness of fit to CXB data from NuSTAR. The x-axis is axion mass m_a in keV (converted to eV: multiply by 1000). The y-axis is g_agamma in GeV^-1. The excluded region is ABOVE the boundary (gray shaded area labeled 'freeze-in'). The blue region labeled 'NuSTAR' shows the constraint from NuSTAR data. The light gray region is the constraint from freeze-in axion production. The boundary traced represents the lower edge of the excluded region. Axis multipliers: x-axis has implicit ×1000 eV (keV to eV conversion); y-axis is in units of 10^-11 GeV^-1 based on tick labels.
